contentBlocks.text: This week you investigated forces from every angle: what they are, how they combine, how they create patterns, and how one special kind works without even touching. Let's put it all together.

Quick review: A force is a push or a pull (Day 1). Forces can be balanced (no change in motion) or unbalanced (motion changes) (Day 2). Watching a pattern in an object's motion lets you predict what happens next (Day 3). Magnetism is a force that works without touching, and can attract or repel (Day 4). Walk back through your own home: find one push, one pull, one balanced-force example, one unbalanced-force example, one motion pattern, and — if you have a magnet — one magnetic attract-or-repel example. That's six real examples of everything you learned this week.
Great work investigating forces and motion this week! You've built a real foundation in physical science that scientists and engineers use every day.

objectives: Recall and correctly apply all four force concepts from the week: push/pull, balanced/unbalanced, motion patterns, and magnetism
Identify a real-life example of each concept
materialsNeeded: Optional: a magnet for the final example
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Send the child on the 'six examples' home scavenger hunt described in the lesson.
3. Complete the cumulative review worksheet, which mixes all 4 days' concepts.
4. Discuss any mismatches or uncertain answers together before finishing.
5. Celebrate finishing the first full week of investigation — this pattern (5 days building to a review) is how every unit this year will work.
differentiationTips: Struggling: allow the child to use their Day 1-4 worksheets as a reference during review rather than working from memory alone
Ready for more: ask them to explain WHY each example fits its category, not just to label it correctly
This is a good checkpoint to note which day's concept needs the most re-teaching before moving to next week's unit
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. Kicking a ball = push. 2. A book resting flat on a table = balanced. 3. A swing going back and forth = a repeating motion pattern used to predict what happens next. 4. A magnet pulling a paperclip without touching it = magnetism (attract).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates NGSS 3-PS2-1 through 3-PS2-4 (balanced/unbalanced forces, motion patterns, and non-contact magnetic/electric forces) before the unit moves on, matching the 'consolidate before adding more' pacing established in earlier units this session.

generationData.instructions: Answer each question, drawing on everything you learned this week.

rows.problem: Kicking a ball is an example of a...?
A book resting flat and still on a table has what kind of forces acting on it?
A swing moving back and forth in the same path is an example of a...?
A magnet pulling a paperclip toward it without touching is called...?
